utterances.text: So you went to Ovcara a year before that. Could you explain who you were with on that occasion, since we have information on a ban that was issued at the time, that's why I'm interested in your first visit in 1995.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately a lot of time has passed, and I can't provide an answer to your question as to why we went there the first time. I do remember, however, that we went there in an organised way with an escort, and I believe Mr. Grujic was with me. He must be in possession of more information about that. That was the Croatian commission's visit, and as I stated, I was there, together with Mr. Grujic, but any more than that, I can't say. I believe that it was a commission visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned the escort. What sort of escort was it?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: When we went through Osijek and afterwards we were escorted by the UN, we were escorted by some military personnel up to Ovcara and back. We didn't go through Vukovar, but around it, finally reaching Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say you arrived at Ovcara, where exactly, and what did you see there then?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we passed by the hangars, reaching the point marked by Clyde Snow. He marked it as a mass grave. We saw that spot next to the grove in the photographs with the depression. And we looked at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, that was all you did on that first occasion. You didn't do anything else there, either yourselves or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. We weren't allowed to do anything else, we just came to see. And as far as I remember, we couldn't even take photographs. That was the nature of the visit, if I may say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The location marked by Dr. Snow, I believe it was done on the 28th of October, 1992 when he went there. I believe you had that in mind when he marked off the location?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, that was the first time that someone actually marked off the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Since you weren't with him on that occasion, nevertheless you mention that event today, and I believe you described Mr. Snow as an expert in locating mass graves, and you mentioned his previous experience with such cases and that he was the one who actually established the actual location of the site?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps that at that very time, or maybe even before Snow arrived at the location, there was a newspaper article in a Croatian newspaper containing a statement of a witness who claimed to have escaped the execution at Ovcara, and he described the location of the site in quite some detail, in relation to Ovcara. Do you remember that, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: I have a vague recollection of articles like that being published. And there was one about a person who, as you have suggested, escaped the execution and fled. There must have been an article like that, I'm certain of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I should not imagine that you personally know whether this gave rise to Dr. Snow and his team's visit to the area in order to discover a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was that one witness or some other witnesses too, or another reason altogether. I'm not sure what the decisive factor was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say that this only took a couple of days, and that about two days later, if I understand you correctly, permission was refused to continue work at the site by the local Serbs, as you say. What is your personal knowledge of this? It was probably at the time that you found out or a little later, wasn't it? Was permission issued to Dr. Snow for what he did on the 28th and around those days and then subsequently refused? Do you know how exactly events unfolded back then?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that aspect. I don't know who approved Snow's visit to the site. I don't know how he got there. I'm not sure if it was by UN mediation or someone else. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But you have spoken about that today. You did give some answers to Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: If I may be allowed to clarify, one thing that I knew was that excavations or exhumations were strictly prohibited. That was what I learned, because of the refusal of the local authorities to authorise any exhumations, but that was all I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on what you have told us, this refusal to authorise any exhumations continued until 1995, which is when work was started at the site, and this we have covered in detail today, haven't we?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You probably do remember one thing quite well. When we speak about the local Serbs, let us try to clarify this, I believe Mr. Smith has asked a number of questions, but I believe further clarification is needed. You probably meant the local Serb authorities in the area. Is it not true that this was at the time under the government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina or the autonomous province of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Srem. I think that was what it was called at the time. The president being Goran Hadzic. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: I think you're right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I'll ask you something. You might know for all I know, since you were a member of the commission. There is information to indicate that back in 1993 on the 17th of November in Erdut, more specifically a meeting was held with the head of your own commission in attendance as well as some other people, including Goran Hadzic. There is information indicating that he authorised for excavations to begin in March or April the following year. Does this ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I would like to go now to the beginning of the dig at Ovcara. Were you there personally from day one? Did you attend when they first started digging?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: As I said before, I went there several times. At the very outset and then I came later. I attended several times during the actual work up until the very end. I saw all the stages; this took over 60 days. I wasn't there every day. There was another colleague of mine who went regularly, and I would just pass by every now and then to see how things were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That precisely is the gist of my question. Was anyone standing in for you? Was there always someone present as an observer for the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a deputy, Dr. Baricevic, who usually travelled on behalf of our commission. For all I know, he was there all the time or most of the time at any rate. I can't vouch for every single day, but he certainly spent most of the time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. It had been agreed that on behalf of Yugoslavia observers should be present too. Based on what I can tell, two names are mentioned, I'll ask you about these, Dr. Dunjic and Dr. Ratasevic [phoen]. Was there anyone else present; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: I think Dr. Dunjic was there, and Dr. Ratasevic was with me in Zagreb as we were processing all the data, Professor Ratasevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Professor Ratasevic was in Zagreb. I saw that in the report, but he produced a report, we may come to that report a little later, indicating that he was also at the site in Ovcara, possibly not at the same time as you and that was why you never met there. That might be an explanation, because he spent a while at Ovcara too.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: That's entirely possible, but I have nothing to say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You have described today and in your previous testimony the way the bodies were extracted and placed in bags and marked in an ascending order from 1 to 200. My question: When this was done -- you mentioned this took over 60 days. Was this being done all the time or as I heard today when you were looking at a photograph that this was done when everything was dug up, that this was only done then. Can you please explain, or, rather, can you please clarify this procedure, as far as you're familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the intention was to dig the whole thing up, the whole grave, to expose the bodies. And after that to start the second stage, extracting the bodies, placing the bodies into bags. As far as I know, that was the method used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That's how it should have been, based on an agreement that was made at the outset, right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR STRINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, based on the agreement, and based on what I personally witnessed there, and based on what I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think we're just about to run out of time. We'll be continuing tomorrow. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. We will adjourn now for the day and resume tomorrow at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
